questions.question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact signed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1931__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gandhi-Irwin Pact/Delhi Pact (5th March 1931):

 
 
• Moderate statesmen Tejbahadur Sapru and Jayakar initiated efforts to bring about a rapprochement between Mahatma Gandhi and the government.
 
• Six meetings with Viceroy Lord Irwin finally led to the signing of a pact between the two to join the Second Round Table Conference.
 
• Regarding Gandhi- Irwin Pact, Jawahar Lal Nehru remarked, ‘*This is the way the world ends, not with a bang but a whimper*.
 
• It was signed before the Second Round Table Conference in London.
 
• It marked the end of the Civil Disobedience Movement in India against the British rule that Gandhi and his followers had initiated with the Salt March.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Lord Irwin (1926 AD-1931 AD):

 
 
• Simon Commission visited India in 1928.
 
• Nehru Report, 1928.
 
• Lahore Session of the Congress, (1929) and Poorna Swaraj, declaration.
 
• Civil Disobedience Movement, 1930 started.
 
• Dandi March (12 March 1930).
 
• Gandhi-Irwin Pact, 5 March 1931.
 
• Sharda Act, 1929, under which the marriageable age of girls (14 years) and boys (18 years) was raised.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhash Chandra Bose founded the Independence of India League.

questions.question: The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022 belongs to _____ Ministry of Indian Government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**External Affairs.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct answer is option 3, i.e., External Affairs Ministry of Indian Government.**
 
• The Weapons of Mass Destruction and their Delivery Systems (Prohibition of Unlawful Activities) Amendment Bill, 2022 **aims to regulate and prohibit unlawful activities related to weapons of mass destruction and their delivery systems.**
 
• The bill seeks to strengthen** India's compliance with international norms** and obligations related to non-proliferation and disarmament.
 
• The bill will also help in preventing the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction to non-state actors or terrorist organizations.
 
• Finance Ministry is responsible for managing the financial resources of the government, Civil Aviation Ministry is responsible for the administration of civil aviation in India, and Defence Ministry is responsible for the defence of India's borders and sovereignty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Weapons of Mass Destruction (WMD) refers to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear weapons that have the potential to cause mass destruction and loss of life**.
 
• The use, development, and proliferation of WMD is a major threat to global peace and security.
 
• The External Affairs Ministry is responsible for India's foreign relations, including its engagement with international organizations and forums related to disarmament, non-proliferation, and arms control.
 
• The Finance Ministry is responsible for managing the financial resources of the government, including budgeting and taxation.
 
• The Civil Aviation Ministry is responsible for the administration of civil aviation in India, including the regulation of air transport services and airport infrastructure.

questions.question: Which is the first month in the Islamic lunar calendar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4__**, Muharram.**__

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Muharram is the first month of the Islamic lunar calendar and is considered one of the four sacred months in Islam.
 
• It is a month of mourning for the Shia Muslims as they commemorate the martyrdom of Imam Hussain, the grandson of Prophet Muhammad, on the 10th day of Muharram.
 
• Shawwal is the 10th month of the Islamic lunar calendar and is significant as it marks the end of the holy month of Ramadan, during which Muslims observe fasts and offer prayers.
 
• Safar is the second month of the Islamic lunar calendar and is considered an unlucky month by some Muslims due to historical events that occurred during this time.
 
• Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar and is considered the holiest month in Islam. It is a time for spiritual reflection, charity, and fasting from dawn until sunset.
 
• Hence, the statement "Muharram is the first month in the Islamic lunar calendar" is correct.

questions.question: As per the Preamble of Indian constitution, India is a ______ country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Republic.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the preamble to the Indian Constitution, India is a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic state.
 
• ​Key Words In The Preamble:
 
• Sovereign:
 
 
• The term Sovereign which is proclaimed by the Preamble means that India has its own independent authority and it is not a dominion of any other external power.
 
• In the country, the legislature has the power to make laws which are subjected to certain limitations.
 
 
 
• Socialist:
 
 
• The term Socialist was added in the Preamble by 42nd Amendment, 1976 which means the achievement of socialist ends through democratic means.
 
• It is basically a Democratic Socialism that holds faith in a mixed economy where both the private and public sectors co-exist side by side.
 
 
 
• Secular:
 
 
• The term Secular was incorporated in the Preamble by 42nd Constitutional Amendment, 1976 which means that all the religions in India get equal respect, protection and support from the state.
 
 
 
• Democratic:
 
 
• The term Democratic implies that the Constitution of India has an established form of Constitution which gets its authority from the will of the people expressed in an election.
 
 
 
• Republic:
 
 
• The term Republic indicates that the head of the state is elected by the people directly or indirectly.
 
• 
 
In India, the President is the head of the state and he is elected indirectly by the people.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Socialist and Secular were the two words added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment, in 1976.

 
 
• The earlier description of India was the Sovereign Democratic Republic.
 
• It was then changed to Sovereign, Socialist, Secular Democratic Republic.

questions.question: What is the term of State legislative assembly in India as per Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __5 years__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• State Legislative Assemblies are analogous to Lok Sabha.
 
• The term is of State Legislative Assemblies is Five Years.
 
 
• Each Legislative Assemblies in India is formed for a period of five years, after which all seats are up for election.
 
 
 
• A person must not be less than 25 years of age to become a member of State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• Money bills can be introduced in the state legislative assembly only with the prior recommendation of the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• State Legislative Assemblies are also known as Vidhan Sabhas.
 
• State Legislative Assembly is chaired by the speaker.
 
• The Governor can summon and prorogue the state legislation and dissolve the state legislative assembly.
 
• State Legislative Assembly is directly elected by the people.
 
 
• Each Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA) is directly elected to serve 5-year terms by single-member constituencies.

questions.question: Which among the following acids makes the pH of vinegar acidic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Acetic__.

__
 
• Vinegar is a sour liquid that is made by the fermentation of numerous dilute alcoholic liquids into a liquid containing acetic acid__.
 
• Vinegar can be made from any liquid that is capable of being converted into alcohol in a two-step process. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The fruit juice or other liquid contains sugar, which is converted into alcohol and carbon dioxide gas by the actions of yeast enzymes.
 
• The alcohol thus formed combines with atmospheric oxygen by the action of Acetobacter bacteria, forming acetic acid and water.
 
• The more aged the vinegar, the deeper the flavour. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Types:

 
 
• There are many types of Vinegar which include apple cider, Balsamic, champagne, distilled white, malt, rice, sherry, and red and white wine vinegar, among others.
 
 
 
• Uses: 
 
 
• Because of its acetic acid content and low pH, vinegar is used as a preservative for both domestic use and in the food industry. 
 
• It is used for the preservation, or pickling, of a wide variety of foods such as vegetables, meat, fish products, and spiced fruits. 
 
• Floral vinegar is an easy way to preserve the vibrant flavours and aromas of edible flowers.
 
• Vinegar adds acidic taste and helps to balance flavour in recipes.

questions.question: According to the 2011 census, what is the approximate female literacy rate?

questions.question: The materials, through which things cannot be seen, are called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Opaque materials.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• We cannot able to see through some materials, such materials are called Opaque.
 
• Substances that do not pass light through them are called Opaque substances.
 
• Objects on the other side of the opaque objects cannot be seen at all. 
 
• Examples are stone, cardboard, wood, metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

__Transparent__

__
 
• Substances that allow light to pass through them completely are called Transparent substances.
 
• Objects on the other side of the transparent objects can be seen clearly.
 
• Examples are glass, water, air. 

Translucent__

 
• Substances that allow light to pass through them partially are called Translucent substances.
 
• Objects on the other side of the translucent objects can be seen, but not very clearly.
 
• Examples are oil paper, tissue paper.

questions.question: In cricket, hitting the ball over the boundary on the full equals ______ runs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hitting the ball over the boundary on the full in cricket is called a "six".**
 
• It means that the batting team** scores six runs.**
 
• This is the highest number of runs that can be** scored off a single ball.**
 
• If the ball bounces before going over the boundary, it is worth four runs instead (called a "four").

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Cricket is a popular sport played in many countries around the world, particularly in England, Australia, India, and the West Indies.
 
• The objective of the game is for one team to score more runs than the other by hitting the ball and running between two sets of wickets.
 
• A boundary is the edge of the playing field, and hitting the ball over it is a common way to score runs quickly.
 
• In addition to fours and sixes, there are other ways to score runs in cricket, such as by running between the wickets or through penalties assessed to the fielding team.

• Article 22 of the Indian constitution provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.__
 
• Though the police have been given various powers for facilitating the making of arrests, the powers are subject to certain restraints.

• The arrested person has the right to be informed at the time of arrest of the offence for which the person is being arrested.

questions.question: The British Parliament passed the Regulating Act in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1773__.

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

 
• Regulating Act 1773:

 
 
• The regulating Act of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal.
 
• This act was passed due to the misgovernment by the British East India government that introduced a situation of bankruptcy and the government had to interfere with the affairs of the Company.
 
• This act permitted the company to retain its territorial possessions in India but sought to regulate the activities and functioning of the company.
 
• It did not take over power completely, hence called ‘regulating’.
 
• The act provided for the appointment of a Governor-General along with four Councillors in the Presidency of Fort William (Calcutta), jointly called the Governor-General in Council.
 
• As per this, Warren Hastings was appointed as the Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William.
 
• A Supreme Court was established at Fort William, Calcutta. Sir Elijah Impey was the first Chief Justice.

questions.question: The Airavatesvara Temple in Tamil Nadu was built by ______.

• This temple is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, along with the Thanjavur Temple, and the Gangaikondacholisvaram Temple.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Rajaraja Chola I**, on the other hand, is known for building the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur, another UNESCO World Heritage Site. This temple is considered one of the greatest achievements of the Chola dynasty and is known for its towering vimana (tower).
 
• **Maharaja Pratap Singh **was a ruler of the kingdom of Jaipur in Rajasthan. He is known for building several palaces and forts in the region, including the famous Hawa Mahal in Jaipur.
 
• ** Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II** was also a ruler of Jaipur and is known for his contributions to astronomy and mathematics. He built several observatories, including the Jantar Mantar in Jaipur, which is still in use today.

 [IMAGE: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/A_different_view_of_Airavatesvara_Temple.jpg/250px-A_different_view_of_Airavatesvara_Temple.jpg]

questions.question: Savings deposits with Post Office savings banks are included in which measure of money supply?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __M2__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India releases data for M1, M2, M3, and M4—four different measurements of the money supply.
 
• The Post Office Savings are thus only included in M2 and M4.
 
• The Post Office Savings Account (SB) is comparable to any savings account offered by a retail bank.
 
• The minimum deposit amount is $500 and the minimum withdrawal amount is just $50. It offers a 4% interest rate.
 
• A savings bank account can be opened by both adults and minors.
 
• The M2 measurement of the money supply in India includes the savings deposits of post office savings banks, which gives it a bit more rigidity than the M1 measurement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• M1, M2, M3, and M4 were the four monetary aggregates that the RBI used to calculate the money supply between 1977 and 1998.
 
• The idea of Reserve Money was also utilised by the central bank.
 
• In India, the post office offers a deposit programme called the post office savings account. 
 
• To calculate and gauge the total supply of money in the market, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) divides currency into four major categories, sometimes referred to as monetary aggregates. M0, M1, M2, and M4 are the numbers.

questions.question: Kajari is a folk song and dance genre of India. It has its roots in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Uttar Pradesh.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Kajri Folk Song is related to Uttar Pradesh __as well as Bihar.
 
• Kajri folk song is often used to describe the longing of a maiden for her lover as the black monsoon cloud arrives in the summer skies, and the style is notably sung during the rainy season.
 
• Kajri folk song is traditionally sung in the villages and towns of Uttar Pradesh around Banaras, Mirzapur, Mathura, Allahabad, and the Bhojpur regions of Bihar.
 
• Maand Folk Song is the traditional folk song of Rajasthan whereas Koli and Lavani Folk Songs belong to Maharashtra and Himachal Pradesh is enriched with the great folk song Jhoori.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Kerala is known for its traditional dance forms such as Kathakali and Mohiniyattam, which are quite different from Kajari.
 
• West Bengal has a rich tradition of folk music and dance forms, including Baul, Jhumur, and Chhau, but Kajari is not one of them.
 
• Punjab is known for its energetic and vibrant Bhangra dance form, which is quite different from the graceful and melodious Kajari.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is the correct answer as Kajari has its roots in this state and is still widely performed here.
